practices.practice: Read the cluster connection URI from an environment variable at runtime and do not commit it to source control; provide a .env.example with a placeholder.
practices.prior_belief: Read the connection URI only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never hard-code or commit it. Provide a .env.example with a placeholder value.

practices.practice: Create one MongoClient per process and reuse it as a singleton rather than creating a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Create a single MongoClient/connection and reuse it as a process-wide singleton (do not open a new client per request).

practices.practice: Always enable TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Require TLS/SSL for connections and verify server certificates (use the w=ssl or tls options appropriate to your driver) and avoid disabling certificate validation.
practices.source_name: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID (azure-resource-manager-bicep)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB TLS required connection string tls=true

practices.practice: For long-lived production secrets, store credentials in a secure secret store such as Azure Key Vault (or prefer Microsoft Entra ID / managed identity + RBAC when supported) and load them at runtime rather than committing them or using plain environment variables for long-lived secrets.
practices.prior_belief: Store production DB credentials in a secure secret store (Azure Key Vault) and load them at runtime instead of environment variables for long-lived production secrets.
practices.source_name: Secure your Azure Key Vault secrets
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB credentials Key Vault best practices

practices.practice: Use least-privilege database users or Microsoft Entra ID roles: create a per-app user/role limited to the sample database rather than using a cluster admin key for application workloads.
practices.prior_belief: Use least-privilege database users: create a user/role limited to the sample_customer_360_08 database with only the permissions required (read, write on specific collections), do not use the cluster admin key for the app.

practices.practice: Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules or Private Link / private endpoints and avoid enabling wide public access for production clusters.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the cluster by restricting network access: enable firewall rules/VNet service endpoints to only allow trusted client IPs or VNet ranges to connect.
practices.source_name: Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB firewall Private Link firewall rules

practices.practice: Design and create compound indexes that match your aggregation/query patterns (e.g., a compound index on customer_id then timestamp to accelerate per-customer recency and sort-by-timestamp queries).
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes that match your aggregation pattern: add a compound index on (customerId, eventDate) to accelerate recency and frequency aggregations and to support sorts by eventDate per customer.

practices.practice: Index the category field (or create a compound index with customer_id when filtering by both) to make category-affinity grouping/lookup efficient.
practices.prior_belief: For category-affinity calculations, index the category field (or use a compound index with customerId if queries filter by both) so grouping/lookup by category is efficient.

practices.practice: When computing metrics or running aggregations, project only the required fields (use $project) to reduce I/O and network transfer.
practices.prior_belief: When computing metrics that only need a subset of fields, always project to return only required fields in aggregation ($project or pipeline projection) to reduce IO and network transfer.

practices.practice: Use explain("executionStats") or the MCP explain_operation tool to inspect aggregation / query plans and iterate index design based on actual explain output and executionStats.
practices.prior_belief: Use explain() or the MCP/monitoring tooling to verify aggregation query plans and confirm the aggregation uses the intended indexes; iterate index design based on actual query plans.

practices.practice: Handle transient errors (including 429 rate-limited responses) with retries and exponential backoff and respect server-provided retry guidance when present.
practices.prior_belief: Handle transient errors (network blips, 429 RateLimit) by implementing retries with exponential backoff; respect server-provided Retry-After or equivalent headers when available.

practices.practice: When writing an assigned segment back to a customer document, perform an atomic single-document update (updateOne with $set or findAndModify) rather than a read-modify-write cycle to avoid race conditions.
practices.prior_belief: When writing the assigned segment back to the customer document, perform an atomic update (updateOne with $set or findOneAndUpdate) rather than read-modify-write to avoid race conditions.
practices.source_name: Updating data in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: For stronger concurrency control when multiple writers may update the same profile, use optimistic concurrency (etags / _etag + If-Match) or include a version field in the update filter.
practices.prior_belief: For stronger concurrency control when multiple agents may update the same profile, use optimistic concurrency (include a version field or etag and require it in the update filter) or use findOneAndUpdate with upsert=false and an appropriate filter.

practices.practice: Use bulk writes/inserts (insertMany / bulk APIs, unordered where appropriate) when seeding or ingesting many events to improve throughput and reduce RU cost.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk writes/inserts (ordered=false, bulk_write) when seeding or loading many events to dramatically improve ingestion throughput and reduce RU consumption.
practices.source_name: Optimize write performance in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: insertMany ordered=false insert bulk Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Provision throughput and monitor RU/s consumption for your database and collections; use autoscale or adjust RU allocation if heavy aggregations or vector searches cause throttling.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput and monitor RU/s consumption for the sample_customer_360_08 database; use autoscale or adjust RU allocation if aggregations or vector searches are causing throttling.
practices.source_name: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB RU consumption autoscale monitor

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes on event collections to automatically expire very old or ephemeral events (create a TTL index on the timestamp field) to control storage growth.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes on the events collection for ephemeral or very old events (create a TTL index on the eventDate field) to automatically prune old documents and control storage/growth.

practices.practice: Limit aggregation result sizes and use server-side pagination ($limit/$skip or better cursor-based paging) to avoid transferring very large result sets to the client.
practices.prior_belief: Limit aggregation result size and use server-side pagination for any query that may return many customers; avoid transferring huge result sets to the app in one call.
practices.how_found: aggregation pipeline pagination limit skip Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Cache configuration or segmentation rules in application memory or an external cache and refresh only when changed (or use integrated/Redis caches) to reduce read latency and RU consumption rather than reading rules from the DB on every invocation.
practices.prior_belief: Cache segmentation rules in application memory and reload them only when changed (e.g., watch a config version field); do not read rules from DocumentDB on every prompt invocation to reduce latency and RU cost.
practices.source_name: Improve efficiency of reads by using a cache with Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB caching patterns cache config avoid DB on every request

practices.practice: For vector search store vectors in a dedicated field with consistent dimensionality, normalize embeddings when using cosine similarity, and record embedding model + dimensions as metadata.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, ensure vectors are stored in a dedicated field with consistent dimensionality and normalized if using cosine similarity; create the appropriate vector index (HNSW/DiskANN/IVF) and set index parameters (M, efConstruction, efSearch) to match accuracy/latency needs.

practices.practice: When creating vector indexes, select the index type (DiskANN, HNSW, IVF) appropriate to scale and explicitly specify the similarity/distance metric (COS, L2, IP) to match how you process/normalize vectors.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes, explicitly specify the distance metric (cosine, dot, or L2) consistent with how you compute/normalize vectors at query time to avoid mismatched results.

practices.practice: Monitor and rotate long-lived credentials regularly and automate rotation (Key Vault supports rotation and dual-key rollover patterns to enable zero-downtime switches).
practices.prior_belief: Monitor and rotate long-lived credentials regularly; when rotating keys, use a two-key rollover pattern so the app can switch without downtime.
practices.source_name: Automate the rotation of a secret for resources that have two sets of authentication credentials
practices.how_found: Key Vault secret rotation dual-key rollover tutorial

practices.practice: Version your document schema (schemaVersion) and store segment labels in clear fields (e.g., segments.current and segments.history) to enable backward-compatible schema evolution and lazy per-document migration.
practices.prior_belief: Keep customer profile schema backward-compatible: store segment labels in a named field (e.g., segments.current and segments.history array with timestamps) instead of mutating unrelated fields.

practices.practice: Run unit and integration tests against a dedicated test database or local emulator and do not run tests against production clusters; use shared/dev throughput or emulator for cost-effective test runs.
practices.prior_belief: Use unit and integration tests against a dedicated test database (e.g., sample_customer_360_08_test), seed known data, and clean up test documents; do not run tests against production clusters.
practices.source_name: Optimize development and testing cost in Azure Cosmos DB
practices.how_found: Azure Cosmos DB testing emulator shared throughput dev test guidance

practices.practice: Instrument and log key metrics (RU consumption, latency, 429 rates, index usage) and include correlation IDs in logs to trace API/DB operations for debugging and alerting.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and log key metrics (RU consumption, latency, 429 rates, index usage) and include correlation IDs in logs so CLI and FastAPI requests can be traced to DB operations.

practices.practice: Don't store unbounded/high-cardinality event arrays inside frequently-updated customer profile documents; keep events in a separate events collection and pre-aggregate or summarize into a small profile document to avoid hot documents and large update costs.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid storing high-cardinality or unbounded arrays directly in the customer doc for frequently updated event data; keep events in a separate collection and compute metrics with aggregation or pre-aggregate into a summary collection to reduce hot documents and RU costs.
